subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB463 LANDED - ALL THREE OF GR38'S LEGS, AND THE MAXIMUM SIZE THEY ARE ALL STATED AGAINST. Citations re-checked on this tree: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "If integer-2 is specified, the length of data-name-3 is set to integer-2" -> OK (General rules 38); "If the amount of storage required to expand the size of data-name-3 is not available, the size of data-name-3 is not changed" -> OK (same rule); cite.py --check 8.5.1.10.1 "The maximum size of a dynamic-length elementary item is smallest of:" -> OK (General); cite.py --check 13.18.19.4 "If the LIMIT phrase is not specified, the maximum number of characters that can be contained by the subject of the entry is implementor-defined." -> OK (General rules 2). WHAT WAS WRONG: every leg of GR38 is stated against "the maximum size of data-name-3", and for an item written WITHOUT a LIMIT phrase this compiler had no such thing. DataItem.DynLengthLimit was the LIMIT phrase with -1 meaning "no phrase", CobolDynString.SetSize's clamp was guarded by `limit >= 0`, and so an unbounded item skipped the clamp and fell into two UNCHECKED long->int narrowings. MEASURED on this worktree's own build before the fix, at --std 2023 with EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL CHECKING ON: `01 WS-D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.` with SET SIZE OF WS-D TO 4294967306 (= 2**32 + 10) printed LEN=000000000010 and 31 spaces for FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS - a ten-character item nobody asked for, exit 0 - and the same declaration with 3000000000 (> int.MaxValue, < 2**32) narrowed NEGATIVE and threw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException out of _PRG_...__Dispatch. WHAT LANDED: 8.5.1.10.1's "smallest of" is now a real computation in ONE place, CobolDynString.MaxSizeOf(Int128?) - the LIMIT phrase read WIDE (so a literal past int is compared at its written value instead of being dropped by an int.TryParse that left the item unbounded) bounded by CobolDynString.MaxLength = 0x3FFFFFDF, the implementor maximum (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 row DOC-A.1-62; the PREFIXED candidate cannot apply because a dynamic-length-structure-name is refused by COBOL1562). DataItem.DynMaxSize carries it to every emitter and defaults to the implementor maximum, so no site can see "no maximum". With that, leg 2 (clamp to the maximum + EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL) is the ONE path for an over-large request - both probes now print LEN=001073741791 EC[EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL] - and the (int) narrowings are exact by construction rather than by inspection. LEG 3 IS IMPLEMENTED RATHER THAN DECLARED UNREACHABLE: the maximum is the carrier's ceiling, not a promise the host can allocate two gigabytes, so an OutOfMemoryException at the growth site returns the item UNCHANGED with the condition set to exist (raised once per statement - a request that already took the clamp leg has set it). Leg 1 (integer-2 -> that length) is unchanged and still pinned by 2023/set_size. The section 7 determination that used to read "always allocatable ... the branch is unreachable ... that third leg never raises" has been rewritten to what the code does; audit_annex_a1.py --check reports no findings.
